capabilities.title: CLI-first password manager backed by GPG encryption and git version control
capabilities.sourceEvidence: gopass: pass-compatible CLI password manager with git integration
capabilities.reason: Nexus is a web dashboard, not a CLI password manager. GPG-based credential storage is outside product scope.

capabilities.title: Git as the sync and audit backend for encrypted secrets
capabilities.sourceEvidence: gopass: secrets stored as GPG-encrypted files in a git repository
capabilities.reason: Private live-vault content must remain local and ignored. Committing encrypted envelopes would create durable metadata, retention, and accidental-disclosure risk in the project repository.

capabilities.title: Hierarchical secret paths: organize secrets in a Unix-style directory tree
capabilities.reason: Sealed records now use validated slash-separated paths with bounded segment depth, stored only inside the encrypted payload and surfaced in the unlocked record index.

capabilities.title: GPG key requirement for all encryption operations
capabilities.sourceEvidence: gopass: requires GPG key pair for encrypt/decrypt
capabilities.reason: Nexus uses browser-native crypto (SubtleCrypto); requiring GPG key management is an unnecessary dependency for the target user.
